claims: The Deep Space Network (DSN) is NASA's international array of giant radio antennas located in California, Spain, and Australia.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) provides continuous two-way communication for solar system exploration.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) provides navigation for solar system exploration.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) provides tracking for solar system exploration.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) is managed by JPL.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) supports robotic missions beyond Earth's orbit.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) supports crewed missions like Artemis beyond Earth's orbit.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) operates 24/7.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) receives data from millions of miles away.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) has three sites placed approximately 120 degrees apart around the globe.
The Goldstone site of the Deep Space Network (DSN) is near Barstow, California.
The Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex in Spain is a site of the Deep Space Network (DSN).
The Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex in Australia is a site of the Deep Space Network (DSN).
The Deep Space Network (DSN) uses large parabolic-dish antennas ranging from 26 to 70 meters.
Deep Space Network (DSN) antennas transmit commands to spacecraft.
Deep Space Network (DSN) antennas receive scientific data.
Deep Space Network (DSN) antennas receive images.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) operates using S-band, X-band, and Ka-bands.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) is transitioning to optical communications using laser.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) communicates with missions throughout the solar system.
The Deep Space Network (DSN) communicates with the Voyager probes.
The Voyager probes are over 15 billion miles away.
The public can view active real-time communications between the Deep Space Network (DSN) and spacecraft via the DSN Now website.
